title: SQuAD: Stanford Question Answering Dataset
description: Reading-comprehension dataset of questions posed on Wikipedia articles, where the answer is a span of text in the passage, plus unanswerable questions in v2.0.
quality_notes: English Wikipedia only, so results here say little about other languages or about text that is messier than an encyclopaedia article.
why_useful: The reference extractive question-answering benchmark, and the dataset most QA tutorials assume you have seen. Small enough to experiment with on a laptop.
learning_outcomes: Frame question answering as span extraction
Read exact-match and F1 as QA metrics rather than as accuracy
size_description: Roughly 100k questions in v1.1; v2.0 adds around 50k unanswerable ones
known_limitations: Answers are always spans present in the passage, which is not how most real questions work
Wikipedia English only, so coverage and register are narrow
access_instructions: Downloadable directly from the dataset page, and packaged on the Hugging Face hub.

title: Large Movie Review Dataset (IMDB)
description: Binary sentiment classification dataset of highly polar movie reviews, split evenly into training and test sets with additional unlabelled data.
quality_notes: Deliberately polarised reviews, so accuracy on it is flattering compared with real-world sentiment data that is mostly ambivalent.
why_useful: The standard first text-classification dataset: small, balanced, and well understood, so your result can be compared against a great deal of published work.
learning_outcomes: Train and evaluate a text classifier end to end
See why a balanced binary task makes accuracy a usable metric
size_description: 50k labelled reviews split evenly between train and test, plus unlabelled data
license: other — the dataset card states "other" rather than a named licence
sensitive_data_notes: Reviews are public user-generated text and may contain offensive language.
known_limitations: Only strongly positive and strongly negative reviews; ambivalent text is excluded by construction
English only, and skewed toward the era in which it was collected
access_instructions: Available from the Hugging Face hub, and from the original Stanford page.

title: UCI Adult (Census Income)
description: Tabular dataset from US census data, used to predict whether an individual's income exceeds a threshold from demographic and employment attributes.
quality_notes: Widely used as a fairness teaching example precisely because it encodes historical inequity. Treat any model trained on it as a demonstration, never as a decision aid.
why_useful: The most common tabular classification dataset, and the one most fairness tooling demonstrates on — which makes it a good place to see how bias analysis actually works.
learning_outcomes: Build a tabular classifier with categorical and numeric features
Measure outcome differences across demographic groups
Explain why a good accuracy score can still describe an unacceptable model
sensitive_data_notes: Contains race, sex, marital status and national-origin attributes derived from census records. Any modelling on it touches protected characteristics, and results should not be presented as findings about people.
known_limitations: Encodes the demographic disparities of the census year it was drawn from
The income threshold is arbitrary and dated
Widely criticised as a fairness benchmark because its framing bakes in the inequity being measured
access_instructions: Downloadable directly from the UCI repository page.

title: MS MARCO
description: Large-scale collection built from real search queries, used for passage ranking, document ranking and question answering over web text.
quality_notes: Large enough that experimenting with the full collection needs real storage and patience. Start with a published subset.
why_useful: Built from genuine search queries rather than constructed ones, which makes it the standard proving ground for retrieval and reranking work.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate a retrieval system with ranking metrics rather than accuracy
Understand the difference between passage and document ranking
size_description: Millions of passages; individual task subsets are much smaller
license: unknown — the site states the data is provided as-is without extending a licence, which is not a standard grant
sensitive_data_notes: Derived from real user search queries. Treat the queries themselves as potentially revealing.
known_limitations: Relevance labels are sparse, so unjudged passages are not necessarily irrelevant
access_instructions: Read the terms on the MS MARCO site before use. The site's wording is not a standard open licence, so confirm what is permitted for your purpose.

title: GLUE Benchmark
description: Collection of nine English sentence-understanding tasks with a shared evaluation platform and leaderboard, spanning inference, similarity and acceptability.
quality_notes: Now largely saturated: modern models score near the ceiling, so a high GLUE number no longer distinguishes much. Useful for learning evaluation, not for claiming state of the art.
why_useful: The clearest way to see what "evaluating a language model" concretely means, because each of its nine tasks is small and inspectable.
learning_outcomes: Explain what a multi-task benchmark measures and what it misses
Recognise benchmark saturation and why it matters
license: other — the Hugging Face card states "other"; constituent tasks carry their own terms
known_limitations: Largely saturated, so headline scores compress near the top
Each constituent task has its own provenance and licence, which the aggregate hides
access_instructions: Available through the Hugging Face hub. Check the terms of each constituent task separately.

title: CoNLL-2003 named entity recognition
description: Newswire text annotated with person, organisation, location and miscellaneous entity spans, in English and German.
quality_notes: The original project page at clips.uantwerpen.be no longer resolves, so the Hugging Face card is the practical entry point. Provenance of the underlying newswire text is worth establishing before any use beyond experimentation.
why_useful: The reference NER dataset, and the one nearly every published entity-recognition score is measured against, which makes your own numbers comparable.
learning_outcomes: Frame entity recognition as sequence labelling
Read span-level precision, recall and F1 rather than token accuracy
size_description: Around 22k sentences in the English portion
license: other — the dataset card states "other" rather than a named licence
sensitive_data_notes: Contains named real people and organisations drawn from news reporting.
known_limitations: Newswire register only, so performance does not transfer to informal text
Four coarse entity types, which is far less than most real extraction tasks need
Dated: entities and world knowledge reflect the period the news was written
access_instructions: Check the dataset card for terms. The underlying newswire text may carry conditions separate from the packaged dataset, so establish provenance before using it beyond experimentation.

title: CNN / Daily Mail summarisation
description: News articles paired with the bullet-point highlights written for them, used as a reference dataset for abstractive and extractive summarisation.
quality_notes: The licence shown on the dataset card covers the packaging. The underlying news articles are journalistic content with their own rights, which the card's tag does not settle — establish that separately before any use beyond experimentation.
why_useful: The standard summarisation dataset, and a useful lesson in metric limitations: ROUGE rewards overlap with the reference rather than a genuinely good summary.
learning_outcomes: Train or evaluate a summarisation model against references
Explain why ROUGE agrees poorly with human judgement
license: apache-2.0 (as tagged on the dataset card; see caveats)
sensitive_data_notes: News reporting about identifiable real people and events.
known_limitations: Highlights are editorial teasers, not faithful summaries, so the references are noisy targets
Strong lead bias: copying the first few sentences scores surprisingly well
access_instructions: Available through the Hugging Face hub. Confirm the rights position of the underlying articles before using it for anything beyond experimentation.
